items.title: Jackson Hole symposium opens with Fed chair's first keynote
items.summary: The Kansas City Fed's annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium runs Aug. 27-29 with the theme Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy. The conference is closely watched as a venue for central-bank signalling, with the U.S. Federal Reserve chair set to deliver the keynote address in his first Jackson Hole appearance in the role.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

items.title: Champions League league phase draw takes place in Monaco
items.summary: UEFA holds the league phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League in Monaco from 18:00 CET on Thursday Aug. 27, allocating 36 clubs into eight matchdays across the new single-league format. The fixture list with kick-off times is due to be published no later than Saturday Aug. 29, with matchday one starting on Tuesday Sept. 8.

items.title: Marvell Technology reports Q2 FY27 earnings after the close
items.summary: Marvell Technology is scheduled to release fiscal second-quarter 2027 results after the U.S. close on Aug. 27, with analysts estimating non-GAAP earnings per share of about 0.93 dollars, up 39 percent year over year, on roughly 2.71 billion dollars in revenue. The print comes roughly a week after Marvell disclosed a 7 percent warrant to Google tied to the custom AI silicon work the chipmaker is doing around Google's Tensor Processing Unit program.

items.title: Cloudflare open-sources Cloudflare OS for corporate AI apps
items.summary: Cloudflare released Cloudflare OS under the Apache 2.0 licence, packaging a capability-based security model on top of its open-source workerd runtime and V8 isolates. Each user gets their own copy of every generated application, with Gatekeeper-mediated access to enterprise resources, and the company says its own staff built more than 4,000 internal tools in the 30 days before the public release.

items.title: CNCF graduates Kubeflow as a cloud-native AI standard
items.summary: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation promoted Kubeflow from incubating to graduated status, marking it as a mature, production-ready platform for running AI and machine-learning workloads on Kubernetes. The project, originally created at Google in 2017, has accumulated more than 33,000 GitHub stars across its repositories and roughly 260 million PyPI downloads for its Python packages, with Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Red Hat, LinkedIn and Spotify among the named adopters.

items.title: IBM releases Granite 4.2 with native reasoning on Hugging Face
items.summary: IBM published its Granite 4.2 large language models on Hugging Face under open weights, alongside a technical deep dive on how the models were built. The release adds a native reasoning capability tuned for enterprise agent workflows and is also available via Ollama and GitHub, with a separate Hypernova-60B model shipped at the same time.

items.title: Premier League clubs finalise moves as the transfer window narrows
items.summary: Premier League clubs continued to finalise squad moves through Aug. 26, with Aston Villa announcing Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal and Aaron Wan-Bissaka's loan to West Ham, alongside Coventry City's additions of Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest and Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United. The summer window closes at 23:00 UK time on Sept. 1, with most clubs still working on at least one late deal before the deadline.

items.title: Rackspace Cloud launches on VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1
items.summary: Rackspace Technology launched Rackspace Cloud, a fully managed multitenant platform built on Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, with initial availability in Dallas followed by Northern Virginia and Chicago. The company frames the launch around demand for governed private infrastructure, citing Broadcom research that 56 percent of organisations are now running or planning production AI inferencing in a private cloud.

items.title: US second-quarter GDP rises 1.5% as consumer spending accelerates
items.summary: U.S. second-quarter gross domestic product rose 1.5 percent, down from 2.1 percent in the first quarter, with consumer spending accelerating to 3.2 percent from 0.5 percent earlier. Private domestic demand, excluding trade, government spending and inventories, expanded at a 3.9 percent annualised rate, illustrating how household outlays rather than net exports did most of the work in the quarter.

items.title: Shopify CEO Lütke ships walgit, an S3-native Git server
items.summary: Shopify chief executive Tobias Lütke released walgit, an open-source database-free Git server written in Rust that runs directly on top of S3-compatible object storage. The initial release on Aug. 24 supports Git's bundle-uri mechanism for distributing large repositories via object storage or CDNs, Git LFS, a built-in web interface and OIDC authentication, with no leader node and no relational database dependencies.

items.title: KubeRay 1.7 lands with a History Server and stronger security
items.summary: The KubeRay project released versions 1.6 and 1.7 of its Kubernetes operator for Ray distributed workloads, adding a beta History Server that retains cluster and job logs after a RayCluster is deleted. The 1.7 release also brings native Kubernetes NetworkPolicy support, automated mTLS via cert-manager, RayCronJob scheduling and an embedded RocksDB backend that removes the external Redis dependency for GCS fault tolerance.

items.title: Apple splits its latest silicon push between M6 and M5 Ultra
items.summary: Apple introduced M6 for the Mac mini and M5 Ultra for Mac Studio, framing both chips around higher performance and expanded AI compute. The two-track launch shows local model workloads becoming a central measure of desktop hardware progress.

items.title: LASK overturns Celtic’s four-goal cushion in a dramatic European exit
items.summary: Celtic went out of Champions League qualifying after LASK reversed a four-goal aggregate deficit. The Austrian side’s 5-1 second-leg win turned a seemingly secure tie into one of the round’s most striking reversals.

items.title: OpenAI publishes first Jalapeño inference results
items.summary: OpenAI released initial results for Jalapeño, presenting the system as a high-speed, efficiency-focused approach to AI inference. The disclosure shifts attention from training scale toward the cost and throughput of serving models in production.

items.title: NASA adds a next-generation dish to deep-space communications
items.summary: NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory unveiled a new next-generation dish for the Deep Space Network. Expanding the ground system is a reminder that distant missions depend as much on reliable communications capacity as on spacecraft hardware.

items.title: US consumer confidence loses ground in August
items.summary: The Conference Board’s August reading showed US consumer confidence declining. The result adds a softer household signal to the outlook, even as investors continue to weigh inflation, interest rates and labor-market resilience.

items.title: Anthropic funds independent study of AI and wellbeing
items.summary: Anthropic launched a $5 million grant program for independent research into how AI systems affect user wellbeing. The initiative puts evaluation of human outcomes alongside technical performance and safety testing.

items.title: Fernandes and Shaw take the PFA’s top player honors
items.summary: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw won the PFA Player of the Year awards, with Nico O’Reilly and Olivia Smith also recognized. The player-voted honors placed Manchester’s leading performers at the center of the season’s awards night.

items.title: Mantel Capture moves its carbon-removal process to commercial scale
items.summary: MIT-linked startup Mantel Capture demonstrated its carbon-capture technology at commercial scale. The milestone moves the discussion from laboratory performance toward whether industrial sites can deploy lower-cost capture in everyday operations.

items.title: Australia’s official music charts draw a line at fully AI-made tracks
items.summary: Australia’s recorded-music industry will exclude wholly AI-generated tracks from its official charts. The rule separates machine-made releases from chart eligibility while the industry works through authorship, labor and audience-trust questions.

items.title: Amazon prepares to close Mechanical Turk’s long-running task marketplace
items.summary: Amazon is shutting down Mechanical Turk, the human-task service once described by Jeff Bezos as “artificial artificial intelligence.” Its closure marks the end of an early model for combining software workflows with on-demand human judgment.

items.title: Leeds advances at Forest as Brentford scores six in the League Cup
items.summary: Leeds beat Nottingham Forest for the second time in three days to move on in the Carabao Cup, while Brentford defeated Birmingham 6-1. The round paired a quick rematch with the night’s clearest attacking statement.

items.title: Nvidia brings RTX Spark’s game and anti-cheat stack to Gamescom
items.summary: Nvidia used Gamescom to showcase RTX Spark support across upcoming PC games, anti-cheat technology and visual-quality features. The package treats compatibility and competitive integrity as part of the graphics platform, not separate add-ons.

items.title: German business sentiment improves more than expected
items.summary: Germany’s Ifo business-sentiment reading rose more than economists expected in August. The improvement offers a cautiously positive signal for Europe’s largest economy, though survey momentum still has to translate into sustained activity.

items.title: OpenAI turns WebMCP experimentation into a public challenge
items.summary: OpenAI announced a challenge centered on WebMCP, bringing fresh attention to structured ways for AI systems to interact with web capabilities. The format invites practical testing of an emerging interface layer rather than another model-only benchmark.

items.title: Four regional Fed boards backed a higher discount rate
items.summary: Minutes showed that four Federal Reserve bank boards favored raising the discount rate. The split is a useful window into regional inflation concerns, even though the recommendation is distinct from the central bank’s policy-rate decision.

items.title: Taiwan charges nine in alleged AI-server export scheme
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors have charged nine people over the alleged illegal export of high-end AI servers to mainland China. Reporting says employees linked to Nvidia and Super Micro were among those charged, intensifying scrutiny of advanced-computing supply chains.

items.title: 3M and BOE open a joint laboratory for next-generation displays
items.summary: 3M and BOE have opened a joint research laboratory focused on display materials and manufacturing. The programme will work across LCD, OLED and MLED applications, including optical films, adhesives, foldable screens and ultra-narrow bezel processes.

items.title: Asian markets face a cautious open after the US technology sell-off
items.summary: Asian equity futures pointed mostly lower after semiconductor shares pulled the Nasdaq 100 down nearly 1%. Investors were also weighing softer oil, firmer US Treasuries and a heavy calendar of economic data and corporate earnings.

items.title: Chelsea edge Fulham in a five-goal Premier League contest
items.summary: Chelsea beat Fulham 3-2 at Craven Cottage in a match that swung through five goals. Club reports confirm the visitors secured the points after Fulham twice found the net, giving Chelsea their first league win of the new campaign.

items.title: European shares finish little changed as technology stocks weigh
items.summary: European equities ended broadly flat after weakness in technology shares offset gains elsewhere. Markets also tracked uncertainty around Iran-related sanctions and looked ahead to incoming economic data, keeping risk appetite restrained.

items.title: GSA takes a coordinating role in the US post-quantum migration
items.summary: The US General Services Administration says its technology-policy office will help coordinate the federal shift to post-quantum cryptography. The work covers identity and building-access systems as agencies move toward encryption intended to withstand future quantum attacks.

items.title: Malen hat-trick powers Roma past Fiorentina
items.summary: Donyell Malen scored three times as Roma opened their Serie A campaign with a 4-0 win over Fiorentina. Paulo Dybala supplied all three assists for Malen before Niccolo Pisilli added the fourth in a dominant home performance.

items.title: SpaceXAI selects Nvidia Vera CPUs for autonomous AI workloads
items.summary: Nvidia says SpaceXAI will deploy its Vera CPUs for a new generation of autonomous AI applications. The announcement positions the processor, designed around intensive reasoning workloads, inside one of the industry's largest planned compute deployments.

items.title: Alibaba proposes HK$80 billion share placement for AI investment
items.summary: Alibaba proposed placing newly issued shares with non-US investors for an aggregate HK$80 billion, subject to market and other conditions. The company says all net proceeds would fund its full-stack AI capabilities, including expanded infrastructure.

items.title: Google tests medical AI in simulated video consultations
items.summary: Google researchers evaluated AMIE in 300 simulated video consultations covering 100 scenarios and involving professional patient actors and 30 primary-care physicians. The team stresses that no real patients took part and that further validation and safety work are required before clinical use.

items.title: Apple sets unified EU app terms and revises commission structure
items.summary: Apple announced a single set of business terms for developers distributing apps in the European Union, effective 1 October. Under the plan, its per-install Core Technology Fee gives way to a 5% charge on qualifying digital sales made through software obtained beyond the App Store.

items.title: Euro-area consumers trim near-term inflation expectations
items.summary: The ECB's July survey put median inflation expectations at 2.9% for the next 12 months and 2.7% three years ahead, each down 0.1 percentage point from June. Five-year expectations were unchanged at 2.4%, while expected economic growth improved but remained negative.

items.title: GeForce Now adds Firefox to its Windows browser lineup
items.summary: Nvidia has added Firefox support for GeForce Now on Windows, allowing members to launch supported cloud games from the browser without installing the dedicated application. Firefox joins Chrome, Edge and Opera among the service's supported Windows browsers.

items.title: Gemma passes one billion downloads as Google opens a project directory
items.summary: Google says its Gemma model family has passed one billion downloads and spawned more than 100,000 community variants. The company also launched an Awesome Gemma repository intended to catalogue projects, fine-tunes, tutorials and developer tools.

items.title: Hull mark Premier League return with win over Manchester United
items.summary: Hull City beat Manchester United 2-0 in their first Premier League match for nine years. The promoted side secured the result despite holding 28% of possession, giving Sergej Jakirovic's team a winning start against last season's third-place finishers.

items.title: Late Szoboszlai penalty earns Liverpool a point at Newcastle
items.summary: Liverpool opened their Premier League season with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle after Dominik Szoboszlai converted a stoppage-time penalty. Cody Gakpo had cancelled out Harvey Barnes's opener before substitute Joe Willock restored Newcastle's lead.
